interest: This document is valuable to historians as an index of U.S. diplomatic surveillance over Japanese societal, racial, and demographic developments during the late 1930s. It reflects American diplomatic interest in ethnography through cooperation with the Smithsonian Institution to acquire Dr. Neil Gordon Munro's study of the indigenous Ainu, alongside critical geopolitical intelligence on domestic population pressures and emerging Pan-Asianist ideologies predicting the eclipse of Western global dominance.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-45) for decimal file 894.401 (Social Matters: Japan, People), indexing diplomatic records received between November 1936 and August 1938. The register lists three separate communications sent from U.S. consular and diplomatic posts in Tokyo, Yokohama, and Keijo (Seoul) to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE). The entries summarize an anthropological article on the Ainu by Dr. Neil Gordon Munro for the Smithsonian Institution, a valuation report analyzing Japanese surplus population pressures and potential remedies like southward expansion and industrialization, and an analytical report from Keijo transmitting a Japanese magazine article foreseeing a global shift in leadership from white to colored races.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet (Form DS-45) recording three diplomatic communications regarding Japanese social conditions, population pressures, and racial ideology from 1936 to 1938.
subfiles.summary: This State Department List of Papers docket sheet indexes records categorized under decimal file 894.401 concerning Japanese social and population matters from November 1936 through August 1938. It records Tokyo despatch No. 1390 transmitting a Japan Advertiser clipping by Dr. Neil Gordon Munro on the Ainu for the Smithsonian Institution; an unnumbered Yokohama report assessing Japan's surplus population problem and expansionist economic remedies; and Keijo despatch No. 170 enclosing a translation of a Japanese magazine article forecasting a global shift in power to colored races. Each entry provides the paper number, origin post, consular officer, date, routing to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, and related cross-reference numbers.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Social Matters, Japan, People (File 894.401)
